replication.target_description: Reading-condition effect on transformed RMET, controlling ART and ART by condition; literary fiction versus nonfiction, pooled across experiments containing both conditions, mixed model with text nested within experiment and condition.

n.sample_role: Participants in the two final mutually exclusive comparison conditions; analytic sample for the identified mixed-model comparison. Text and experiment are modeled random effects, not participant counts.
n.exclusions: Final post-exclusion participants. Page 3 lists 510 additional recruits excluded for dropping out before text assignment (46), nonoriginal texts (165), noncompletion (284; superscript footnote 1 attached in canonical text), extreme reading times (3), low RMET outlier (1), and high ART guessing (10). These are whole-source exclusion counts, not separately allocated to this comparison; subgroup exclusion details are in unsupplied Tables S5/S6.

reported_success.quote: we found no support for any short-term ... causal effects of reading literary fiction on theory of mind.

notes:
Original locators refer to p. 2/Table 1 or Table 2; retrieved Sciencexpress version places both tables on PDF p. 6. Table 2 provides adjusted means, not omega squared; the matching Table 1 condition effect is extracted. 
Completion source review (n_r): Explicit comparison-specific analytic N, supported by Table 1 final condition samples.
Completion source review (es_value_r): Printed adjusted mixed-model condition effect and same-test p; comparator and immediate RMET outcome identify the page-located test.
Completion source review (pval_value_r): Printed adjusted mixed-model condition effect and same-test p; comparator and immediate RMET outcome identify the page-located test.
Completion source review (reported_success): Authors explicitly report failure to support the immediate causal reading effect. This is the paper-level replication verdict, not an inference from p; the authors separately report positive lifetime ART associations. Row-specific test correspondence remains unresolved where stated.
